column3: The Hebrew explicitly calls him a slave and does not add “you” as the recipient of his service.
The second condition says “if he is married,” rather than expressly repeating his arrival with a wife.
The Hebrew emphasizes his declaration and says “I will not go free,” rather than “I do not want to.”
The Hebrew says “to God,” rendered “before the judges.” It describes serving “forever,” rendered “for life.”
The Hebrew uses “her” without separately saying “his first wife.”
The Hebrew preserves “to his hand” in describing what God allowed.
The Hebrew retains the image of finding the kidnapped person “in his hand.”
The Hebrew states that the victim shall surely “be avenged,” rather than directly describing punishment of the master.
The Hebrew says the servant “remains” a day or two, rather than gets up afterward, and literally calls him “his silver.”
The Hebrew has “her children come out,” plural, without expressly adding “prematurely” or “further” before injury.
The Hebrew says “if there is harm” without a separate adjective “serious,” and “you shall give life for life.”
The Hebrew describes the goring as having occurred “yesterday and the day before,” rather than simply naming a habit.
The Hebrew makes payment an obligation when ransom is imposed, rather than saying he “may” redeem his life.
